findings.problem: Nine nearly identical hom_ext proofs (lines 253-270, 287-304 and 315-329) each compute a composite φ ≫ aMap, φ ≫ b1Map or φ ≫ b2Map. Here φ = pullback.lift a r _ : T ⟶ pullback (prodStr g g) g. Every block does the same work. It splits with hom_ext, rewrites with assoc and aMap_fst/b1Map_fst/b2Map_fst, undoes the assoc, and then peels off pullback.lift_fst/lift_snd layer by layer. The long restatements of the same nested pullback.lift term, including its side-proof terms, are copied into every have, three times per face. Only the target differs. A reader has to compare the rw chains one by one to see that they are the same argument, and any change to aMap, b1Map or b2Map has to be repeated in nine places.
findings.proposed_change:
Add three general lemmas in section theta, right after the aMap_fst/…/b2Map_snd simp lemmas.

1. `lift_comp_aMap {T} (a : T ⟶ pullback g g) (r : T ⟶ B) (h : a ≫ prodStr g g = r ≫ g) (h' : (a ≫ addMor g G) ≫ g = r ≫ g) : pullback.lift a r h ≫ aMap g G = pullback.lift (a ≫ addMor g G) r h'`.
2. `lift_comp_b1Map`, with right-hand side `pullback.lift (a ≫ pullback.fst g g) r _`.
3. `lift_comp_b2Map`, with right-hand side `pullback.lift (a ≫ pullback.snd g g) r _`.

Each is proved by `apply pullback.hom_ext` followed by `simp`/`rw` with the existing aMap_fst/aMap_snd (resp. b1Map_*, b2Map_*), using `pullback.lift_fst/lift_snd`.

Also add the corollaries for a = pullback.lift p q hpq, which is the shape in face₁ and face₂. `lift_lift_b1 : pullback.lift (pullback.lift p q hpq) r hr ≫ b1Map g = pullback.lift p r _` and `lift_lift_b2 : … ≫ b2Map g = pullback.lift q r _`. Here pullback.lift_fst/lift_snd collapse `a ≫ fst` to `p` and `a ≫ snd` to `q`.

Rewritten uses:
- face₁: hβ becomes `lift_lift_b1 g _ _ _ _ _`. Its right side is `pullback.lift (G.one _).1 (pullback.snd g g) _`, which is E up to the abbrev `sndPt`. hγ becomes `lift_lift_b2 …`, with right side `pullback.lift (pullback.fst g g) (pullback.snd g g) _` = W. hα is `lift_comp_aMap` followed by one `pullback.hom_ext` whose fst goal is exactly the already-derived `lift_addMor G (G.one _) (fstPt g)` with `G.one_mul`.
- face₂: hα, hβ, hγ are the same three steps with p and q swapped and `G.mul_one` in place of `G.one_mul`.
- face₃: use `lift_comp_aMap/b1Map/b2Map` with a = 𝟙 _. The only residue is `Category.id_comp`, so the three goals reduce to `pullback.lift (𝟙 _ ≫ x) _ _ = pullback.lift x _ _`.

The unique mathematical inputs (`lift_addMor` with `one_mul` / `mul_one`) then stay visible in face₁ and face₂. The `nonempty_pullback_theta` calls and the final `tensor_dual_dual_iso_*` / `triple_iso_unit` steps are unchanged.
findings.benefit: About nine 4-line rewrite chains (roughly 60 lines, most of face₁–face₃) shrink to three small, reusable lemmas plus one-line uses. The faces then read as the group-law computation and the line-bundle isomorphism, not as pullback bookkeeping. The same lemmas can be used for `rigSection_eq`-style computations such as `hs` in `nonempty_pullback_rigSection_theta`. Changes to aMap, b1Map or b2Map need to be fixed only in the lemmas. The face statements already depend on specific `pullback.lift` shapes, so the lemma-based approach also keeps those proofs from being sensitive to the rw order.
